title: One Festival, Many Names
body: In mid-January, on or around January 14, people in many parts of India celebrate the beginning of the harvest season. In many places the day is called Makara Sankranti. In Tamil Nadu, families boil the new rice with milk and jaggery and celebrate Pongal. In Assam, people gather for feasts during Magh Bihu. In Punjab, bonfires are lit for Lohri, and in Gujarat the sky fills with kites on Uttarayan. A map of India showing these celebrations has more than a dozen different names marked on it, all for roughly the same date. The foods, songs and customs differ from region to region, but the occasion being marked is similar everywhere.
